minutes.headline: Water commissioners will seek a grant to repay pilot costs, skip the July funding round and price more water-source options.
minutes.summary: The board reorganized, then spent most of the meeting with Tighe and Bond on next steps after voters rejected the PFAS treatment plan. They agreed to finish the pilot tests, apply for a reimbursement grant, and seek costs for interconnections and other options to put to residents in separate articles. A not-to-exceed retainer for Capital Strategic Solutions was moved from the maintenance budget; the water main project was rescued and water restriction rules were reviewed.

Allocate funds out of maintenance to retain Capital Strategic Solutions and authorize the chairman to sign the proposal

budget_items.what_was_said: A state grant program with newly added funds could reimburse pilot and planning/design costs; the application is rolling and Christie will work on it.
The proposal caps annual spend as an as-needed service rather than a monthly commitment.
The superintendent said the retainer can be paid from the current maintenance budget before July 1, so no new line item is needed.
Escalating fines for violations were discussed, with a question of making them daily.

budget_items.what_was_said: A commissioner suggested taking money from the July 1 budget to hire Tighe and Bond; residents would vote on appropriating funds for more planning.

what_happened.line: Commissioners agreed to finish the pilot tests and apply for a state grant to reimburse pilot and planning costs, as the first step after voters rejected the PFAS treatment plan.
The district will not meet the July 26 funding round; it will finish pilots, gather costs and reapply next year.
Tighe and Bond are to give rough costs for interconnections and other options, with each put to residents as a separate article.
A motion to retain Capital Strategic Solutions was made, to be paid from the existing maintenance budget with no new line; the outcome was not audible.
Revised water-restriction rules, including the wording of daily fines, go to a later meeting; the board also dropped a public records request matter.

why_it_matters: Water-source options may reach residents as separate funding articles at a future town meeting, each with its own cost, rather than as one treatment-plant vote.
The delayed funding round means the water supply question runs another year, and a reimbursement grant may offset part of the pilot costs; whether it does depends on the state's decision.
Proposed escalating fines for water-restriction violations would change what residents face in a drought, once revised rules return.
